Evelyn (CS): FYI — acme reported the rerank endpoint returning identical scores across all candidates for some requests. sometimes a 422, sometimes a payload that succeeds but all scores are 0. customer insists model/config unchanged. pasting their minimal repro curl below.

Rajat (Eng): can you paste the curl + payload? also which model / rerank route?

Evelyn (CS): curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "model": "rwd-re-rank-1",
    "documents": [
      {"id": "d1", "text": "How to index logs", "metadata": {"query": "search logs for error"}},
      {"id": "d2", "text": "Log retention policy", "metadata": {"query": "search logs for error"}}
    ],
    "candidates": [
      {"id": "c1", "text": "error log analysis"},
      {"id": "c2", "text": "retention policy summary"}
    ],
    "query": "search logs for error"
  }'

Evelyn (CS): they said they put their user query inside each document metadata key named `query` because they wanted per-doc context.

Rajat (Eng): ah — that inner metadata key named `query` is colliding with the top-level `query` semantics in our parser. we normalize text fields and fell back to using the first "query" string we see when building candidate vectors. if every doc contains identical metadata.query the feature vector becomes nearly identical -> identical scores. also some of their requests hit our strict payload validator because nested `query` in metadata overlaps reserved path and triggered a 422 on newer validation rules.

Megan (PM): so two issues: (1) ambiguous field name causing semantic collision at serving time, (2) new validator rejecting when nested key matches reserved names. both explain the inconsistent failure modes.

Rajat (Eng): repro steps i used locally: send the payload Evelyn pasted -> scores identical. rename metadata key to `user_context` or `user_query_text` and keep the root-level `query` -> scores vary as expected. i also repro'd the 422 by turning on strict schema validation in the client. minimal diffs below.

Rajat (Eng): diff example (worked):
```json
{"documents":[{"id":"d1","text":"How to index logs","metadata":{"user_context":"search logs for error"}}],"candidates":[{"id":"c1","text":"error log analysis"}],"query":"search logs for error"}
```

Rajat (Eng): failing pattern (ambiguous):
```json
{"documents":[{"id":"d1","text":"How to index logs","metadata":{"query":"search logs for error"}}],"candidates":[{"id":"c1","text":"error log analysis"}],"query":"search logs for error"}
```

Evelyn (CS): customer confirmed renaming metadata key fixed both the 422 and the identical-score issue. they switched to `user_query` and everything returned to normal. :white_check_mark:

Megan (PM): can we add a validator warning that rejects reserved names in metadata or at least logs a clear diagnostic? we should also add a short blurb to the rerank docs about reserved keys and examples.

Rajat (Eng): agreed. i'll file a small infra change to emit a structured warning when metadata contains reserved keys (query, candidates, documents). in the short term, i recommended support send an explanatory note and the sample diff to the customer.

Evelyn (CS): sending note now. ticket #ACME-1427 updated.

support-bot: Escalation created: ACME-1427 -> assigned to Rajat (Eng). SLA: 72h.

Evelyn (CS): leaving this thread open in case any edge cases crop up. thanks all. :pray:
